column1: # CORRECTIONS APPLIED TO THE CORPUS, and who checked them. PLAN.md rule 1: every replacement is

column3: Flexure block made a state variable: carry w_prev (zeros on the first call); t_load = h + w_prev is the UN-deflected rock column; q = ρc·g·t_load; k = sqrt(kx²+ky²); W = FFT2(q)/(D·k⁴ + (ρm−ρinfill)·g); w_new = IFFT2(W); h −= (w_new − w_prev); w_prev = w_new. Prose states that the naive form (load from the already-deflected h, written back over h) converges to zero at 0.15 per call, and that PLAN v1's 'compute w_new from the deflected h and subtract only the increment' converges to h₀/(1+T) = 0.54·h₀ at long wavelength, not (1−T)·h₀ = 0.15·h₀. A failure row for the symptom added. The document still says flexure belongs inside the erosion loop, now with the reason it must be idempotent.
column4: T(k) = ρc·g/(D·k⁴ + Δρ·g). Call 1: w = T·h₀, h = (1−T)·h₀. Call 2: t_load = h + w = h₀, same w, h unchanged — the fixed point is (1−T)·h₀ exactly. Naive: h_{n+1} = (1−T)·h_n → 0 (0.1515^10 = 6.4e-9). v1: Δ_{n+1} = −T·Δ_n, so h_∞ = h₀ − T·h₀/(1+T) = h₀/(1+T); at k=0 that is 1/1.848 = 0.541. Rig: 3000 m Gaussian bump (2-D; a 1-D profile gives 790 m, not the audit's 1163), σ = 60 km, Te = 20 km, ρc = 2800, ρm = 3300, ρinfill = 0, E = 70 GPa, ν = 0.25, 512 cells × 2 km, fftfreq in rad/m; the audit's 512 × 1 km rig gives the same peak to 0.1 m. Naive reproduces the audit to the metre: 1163 → 610 → 387 → 76 m on the 512 x 1 km rig (609.2 on the 2 km rig). VERIFIER additionally required w_prev = IFFT2(T/(1-T) FFT2(h)) for an authored surface already standing at h -- with w_prev = 0 the first call deflects it, which is the very mistake the document's own k = 0 paragraph names; measured a no-op to 3.6e-12 m over three calls. Applied. v1 measured: 1905.1 m after 200 calls against a predicted (1+T)⁻¹h₀ peak of 1905.1 m, max diff 5e-12 m. Scripts: scratchpad/flex.py (all three schemes), scratchpad/gate.py (block extracted from the document by regex and run literally).
column5: PLAN gate max|h − (1−T)·h₀| < 1e-9 m after 10 calls: measured 1.364e-12 m. max|h − h_single_shot| after 10 calls: 2.274e-13 m. Single-shot peak 1163.3 m (audit 1163). Peaks after calls 1..10 all 1163.3 m.

column4: α = [4D/(Δρ·g)]^¼ with D = E·Te³/(12(1−ν²)); D ∝ Te³ so α ∝ Te^(3/4). Recomputed: D(20 km) = 4.978e22 N·m, α = 49.8 km; table matches the audit's to 0.1 km; 512 km / α = 29.1 / 17.3 / 10.3 / 6.1 / 3.6. Raising Te therefore lowers domain/α, the ratio the symptom is defined by.

column3: Block gains the line k = sqrt(kx² + ky²)  # RADIAL wavenumber. The ⚠️ paragraph is retitled '…and make it radial' and states k is the radial magnitude, k⁴ = (kx² + ky²)², and that kx⁴ + ky⁴ is a different, anisotropic operator giving a four-lobed flexural moat nearly twice as deep on the diagonals as on the axes. A failure row 'four-lobed star in the flexural moat' added.
column4: On the 512 x 1 km bump rig (the audit's), moat depth (most negative surface) along an axis vs a diagonal: radial k⁴ gives −93.6 m vs −94.2 m (diag/axis 1.01, circular); kx⁴ + ky⁴ gives −52.2 m vs −96.8 m (diag/axis 1.86). The 512 x 2 km rig reads 1.886 vs 0.999. The audit reported 1.84 vs 0.95 with a different moat metric; the qualitative claim (four lobes, ≈2× on the diagonals) holds, and the document quotes 'nearly twice', which both measurements support. VERIFIER: the ratio is a property of THIS load width, not of the operator -- 1.02 at sigma = 10 km, 1.07 at 20, 1.14 at 30, 1.26 at 40, and a sigma >= 90 km Gaussian has no moat to measure at all. The document was rescoped to say so, and the failure row now reads 'isolated load'; a true point load is anisotropic only in the far field, not in its moat depth.
column5: diag/axis moat ratio 1.86 for kx⁴ + ky⁴ against 1.01 for the radial operator.

column3: The Airy line now names its h as a surface standing at elevation h, with root r = 5.6·h and load column t_load = h + r = 6.6·h. A 'Two symbols, kept apart' paragraph separates surface elevation h from the load column t_load; the flexure block takes t_load. The ⚠️ paragraph replaces 'which is the Airy limit falling out for free' with: T(0) = ρc/(ρm − ρinfill) = 0.85 of the column subsides, leaving the surface at 0.15·t_load; that reproduces Airy only when t_load is the whole column — with ρinfill = 0, 0.1515 × 6.6·h = 1.0000·h; fed the surface h alone the k=0 limit puts the surface at 0.15·h, the mechanism behind X37.
column4: (1 − ρc/(ρm − ρinfill))·(1 + ρc/(ρm − ρc)) with ρinfill = 0 is ((ρm − ρc)/ρm)·(ρm/(ρm − ρc)) = 1 exactly; numerically 0.151515 × 6.6 = 1.0000. With the surface h alone as load the k=0 surface is 0.1515·h, which is the per-call long-wavelength gain of the old block.
column5: k=0 limit of the block reconciles with the Airy line at 1.0000·h when the load is the full column 6.6·h; 0.1515·h when it is not.
